evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches directly into "we just wanted to ask you some information just to make sure that we have the correct details on file" — no time-boxed framing, no promise of a dependable quote, no wait for yes.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep goes straight into logistics: "what is the unit number?" and probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Not applicable — no concerns were raised by the customer.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Not applicable — no concerns were raised to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covered property type (apartment, house), floors (3rd floor, 1 story), bedrooms (3, 3), garage/additional rooms, walking distance (10-20 ft / half minute, 20 ft), and access concerns (no low-hanging trees, steep drives, narrow pathways). Nearly complete.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: "A typical number of boxes between 35 to 45 boxes. Do you feel that you fall within that range?" — Customer confirmed yes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Gave specific dollar amount ($1,554) and time range (6–7 hours) but did NOT anchor it to a typical range for this home size first, nor did rep personalize it to the customer's stated prep level or concerns.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep mentioned 2.5-hour minimum and hourly billing ("you only need to pay for four hours") and no deposit/upfront fees. Did NOT mention trip fee, overnight fee, or materials disclosure upfront; mentioned some fee info only after customer asked.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moved straight from estimate into explaining scope (room placement, disassembly/reassembly) with no pause for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No — rep did not ask 'does that put those to rest?' or close the Two Promises section.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep moved from scope clarification directly to "I'll send you a confirmation email" with no genuine final-concerns check.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked "Would you like our help with your move?" — rep stated "I'll send you a confirmation email" and moved to payment clarification as if the booking was already confirmed.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: "We don't have deposit here or upfront fees. You only need to pay once the job is done, and only for the actual hours." — Rate lock (no upfront deposit) was mentioned.

top_strength: Excellent logistics discovery — rep systematically gathered all seven key details (property type, floors, rooms, walking distance, access concerns, special items, box count) with follow-up clarifications that showed genuine attention to accuracy.
coaching_note: This call skipped Section 1's quid pro quo framing entirely and never asked the customer's concerns, Two Promises, or final objection checks — it read as a confirmation/verification call rather than a sales call, and the explicit ask for business was never made.
